book.title: The Telegraph All New Toughie Crossword, book 1

clue.text: Hats off and briefly state complaint

indicators.note: hats that are off have been knocked out of shape, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: MA is the postal abbreviation of Massachusetts, a US state written briefly

explanation.surface: Someone takes their hat off and grumbles in a few words.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an ailment, and asthma is a chronic breathing disorder of exactly that kind.

clue.text: Everything you said about fascination

indicators.note: the word you is spoken, giving the letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the word you sounds like the letter U
re means concerning, on the subject of

explanation.surface: Everything you said concerned your enthralment.
explanation.definitionFit: Allure is the power of attraction or charm, the quality that fascinates.

clue.text: Quantity of leaf cut up in brew

indicators.note: the letters are stewed together like tea in a pot, so rearranged

explanation.surface: How much tea leaf, chopped up, goes into a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut up' looks like the anagram signal, but those words are letters too; the brew mixes them.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacupful is a measure of volume, the amount one teacup holds.

clue.text: Somebody making blancmange or crumble

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who moulds, since blancmange is set in a jelly mould
second meaning: to decay into dust

explanation.walkthrough: Blancmange and crumble look like two puddings, but the second is a verb. Blancmange is a set milk pudding turned out of a mould.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a person who shapes things in a mould and a verb for decaying slowly.

clue.text: Silver in starry bar framing glass

indicators.note: the symbol for silver sits in the word for starry, enclosed by it

parts.note: astral means relating to the stars

explanation.surface: A sparkling bar with silver fittings around its mirrors and glassware.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads like part of the bar-room scene, but it is a joinery term: the clue's 'bar' is a moulding, not a pub counter.
explanation.definitionFit: An astragal is a glazing bar, the thin moulding that holds panes in a window or cabinet door.

clue.text: Reserved seating for spectators of Formula One's hard

parts.note: a stand is a tiered structure where spectators sit or stand
F is the abbreviation in Formula One, written F1
one gives the Roman numeral, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: Booked seats in the stand for watchers of the Formula One race, which is tough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserved' looks like booked seats, but it describes a person's manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved person keeps others at a distance, aloof and cool, as a standoffish one does.

clue.text: First tyre to get pierced by canine

indicators.note: the tyre word is punctured, with the canine letter driven into it

parts.note: a radial is a radial-ply tyre
C is the dental abbreviation for a canine tooth

explanation.surface: The first tyre to suffer a puncture from a dog's tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: Radical in its root sense means going back to the origin, hence primary.
explanation.definitionFit: Radical describes what is basic or original, coming from the root, so it can stand for primary.

clue.text: Channel regularly failing to show Scripture lesson and a hint of religion

indicators.note: these pieces do not appear, so they are taken out of the word regularly

parts.note: RE is religious education, the school lesson in scripture

indicators.note: only a hint, the opening letter, of the word religion is used

explanation.surface: A TV channel keeps missing its scripture slot and any trace of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like the signal to take alternate letters, but it is the word that loses letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A gully is a channel cut by running water, or a gutter or drain.

clue.text: Guilt, confound it! Sin's involved, the sort you'd wish for at Babel

definitions.text: the sort you'd wish for at Babel

indicators.note: confounding the letters throws them into disorder, rearranging them
the letters are tangled up together, which adds to the rearranging

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry about guilt and sin, then a wish for help at Babel.
explanation.walkthrough: At the Tower of Babel God confounded the builders' language, so a speaker of many tongues would have been handy.
explanation.definitionFit: A linguist speaks many languages, exactly the person needed when everyone's speech was scrambled at Babel.

clue.text: Bond gives French the shivers

parts.note: le is the masculine form of 'the' in French
ague is a fever marked by fits of shivering

explanation.surface: Something about James Bond that unnerves the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007, but it means a union or alliance here.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is an alliance of parties joined by agreement, which is a bond between them.

clue.text: Instrument with mark on dial blurring number

parts.note: M stands for the mark, the former German currency

indicators.note: the words on dial are smudged out of shape, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gauge whose dial has a mark that smears the reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument' and 'dial' suggest a meter, but the instrument is a musical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandolin is a small lute-like musical instrument with paired metal strings, played with a plectrum.

clue.text: Anti-Royalist mistakenly hounded a Republican

indicators.note: the letters are put down in the wrong order, so they need rearranging

explanation.surface: An opponent of the monarchy wrongly harassed a member of the Republican party.
explanation.walkthrough: Roundheads were the Parliamentarians of the English Civil War, named for their cropped hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roundheads fought against King Charles I and his Cavalier supporters, so they were opponents of the Royalists.

clue.text: Recount last of the vote that is cast for Monsieur de Paris

indicators.note: the letters are cast like dice, thrown into a new order
only the final letter of the word the is used

parts.note: X is the cross marked on a ballot paper
i.e. is short for id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A recount of the final vote cast for a Paris official.
explanation.walkthrough: Monsieur de Paris was the official title of the public executioner of Paris; 'cast' looks like voting, but it shakes up the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Monsieur de Paris was the traditional title of France's chief headsman, the state's official executioner.

clue.text: Fur supplier, evasive, turned up

parts.note: coy means reluctant to give details, dodging a question

indicators.note: the word up is turned round, so read backwards

explanation.surface: A dodgy fur dealer finally showed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned up' reads as arrived, but 'turned' works on the word next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu is a large South American rodent farmed for its pelt, sold as nutria.

clue.text: With four grand left to squander, head for oblivion

indicators.note: the letters are scattered like money thrown away, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: With four thousand pounds to blow, someone heads for a drunken stupor.
explanation.walkthrough: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivion is the state of having forgotten or being unaware, the same as total forgetfulness.

clue.text: What's made by yeomen Say isn't hard-earned

definitions.note: a verb phrase; with What's it describes money that comes without effort

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, so rearranged

explanation.surface: The money farmers called yeomen make, Say suggests, comes easily.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'What's ... isn't hard-earned' together: the definition covers whatever comes without effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy money is cash gained with little work, often dishonestly, the opposite of hard-earned wages.

clue.text: In slack times Rocker's rival might be pushy

indicators.note: the rival is placed in the rearranged letters
the letters of times are loosened and fall into a new order

parts.note: Mods and Rockers were rival youth gangs in 1960s Britain

explanation.surface: In quiet periods, a rocker's rival can turn aggressive.
explanation.walkthrough: Mods rode scooters and Rockers motorbikes, and the two cults famously fought at British seaside resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: A pushy person is forward and lacking modesty, which is what immodest means.

clue.text: Crowding us out with what's terribly dim and unlit

indicators.note: the letters are in a terrible mess and must be put back in order

explanation.surface: A crush of people blocks us out from a gloomy, dark place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' between dim and unlit only joins them; it is not part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowding as an adjective describes things thronging in great numbers, as does multitudinous.

clue.text: United player finally forced to make unwelcome appearance

indicators.note: the letters are forced out of shape, so rearranged
only the closing letter of player is used

explanation.surface: A Manchester United player is finally forced to turn up where unwanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude is to push in where one is not wanted, turning up uninvited.

clue.text: Old boy likes knitting needle

indicators.note: the letters are knitted together into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A former pupil who enjoys knitting needs a needle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needle' looks like knitting kit, but it is a stone monument, as in Cleopatra's Needle in London.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelisk is a tall tapering stone pillar; such monuments are called needles.

clue.text: Mean knight would split one and tenpence once

indicators.note: the knight's letter would come between the other pieces, splitting them

parts.note: in pre-decimal money ten pence was written 10d, d being the old penny

explanation.surface: A stingy knight who would divide one shilling and tenpence in old money.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the chess notation for knight. 'Mean' looks like stingy, fitting the money talk, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean to do something is to intend it, to have it as a purpose.

clue.text: It's evident in the state of the needy

indicators.note: the answer sits in the middle of the word, inside its first and last letters

parts.note: poverty is the condition of people in need

explanation.surface: A remark that hardship is plain to see among the poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and plainly visible, not hidden, so it matches evident.

clue.text: Tree that's almost beyond reviving

indicators.note: revived letters are brought back to life in a new arrangement
almost all of the word beyond is used, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: A tree that is nearly too far gone to save.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a tropical hardwood tree yielding the dense black timber of the same name.

clue.text: Mongoose: one and one munch snakes

indicators.note: the letters wind about like a snake, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mongoose and its mate eat snakes, as mongooses famously do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snakes' looks like the thing eaten but is a verb meaning twists.
explanation.definitionFit: The ichneumon is the Egyptian mongoose, a species found across Africa and southern Europe.

clue.text: Dazed queen to admit lecturer is silver-tongued

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in the lecturer's letter, letting it inside
a dazed queen is confused, so the letters of queen to are jumbled

explanation.surface: A bewildered queen lets in a lecturer, who turns out to be persuasive.
explanation.walkthrough: L for lecturer is familiar from the L-plates of a learner, but here it is the lecturer abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A silver-tongued speaker is fluent and persuasive, which is what eloquent means.

clue.text: He's promised with name to provide money

parts.note: to finance something is to fund it

explanation.surface: A man who pledges, in his own name, to put up the funds.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay runs backwards: the answer with N for name added gives a word for providing money, so take that N away.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiancé is a man engaged to be married, someone promised in marriage.

clue.text: Unusual fruit? Try yerba to spice it up

indicators.note: spicing the words up livens them into a new arrangement of their letters

parts.note: yerba is a South American herb brewed as mate tea

explanation.surface: Advice to add yerba to an odd fruit dish to give it more flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: The tayberry is a modern hybrid of blackberry and raspberry, a berry rarely seen in shops.

clue.text: Approved letter in dictionary

indicators.note: the letter's name is placed in the dictionary's abbreviation

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
kay is the spelt-out name of the letter K

explanation.surface: A word that has been given approval for entry in the dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: To okay something is to sanction it, so a thing okayed has been approved.
